messages:
sarah_support: Hey team, a customer (Julie) reported that the CSV they downloaded from Console -> Analytics is truncated at ~12k rows and Excel stops parsing the file after that. They say the raw file size looks normal in the browser's Downloads list but Excel opens only the first chunk. :confused:

customer_julie: Uploaded screenshot — shows Excel stops at row ~12234 and the rest of file is missing when opened. Tried reopening, same result. 

sarah_support: Repro steps from customer: 1) Analytics -> Query -> Export CSV (Apply filters) 2) Browser shows download complete 3) Open in Excel (Windows) -> loads only to row ~12234 4) Open file in VS Code shows more rows but then a strange NUL (�) around byte ~1.4MB then many rows appear unreadable. They attached the downloaded file.

ben_prodeng: Hmm. Can you paste the first 200 bytes around where VS Code shows the NUL? Also which browser/version?

customer_julie: Chrome 113.0.5672 on Windows 10. Here's the hex excerpt she pasted: `...0x1F 0x8B 0x08 0x00 ...` and then later `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00` (lots of zeros). She says the download filename ends with `.csv` not `.csv.gz`.

mike_analytics: Interesting — `0x1F 0x8B` is gzip magic. Looks like at some point bytes are gzipped then served as plain `.csv` without Content-Encoding header. If the file contains a gzip header in the middle it could confuse Excel/CSV parsers and some apps stop on the NUL.

olga_sre: export-bot shows an export job completed successfully: job_id=exp-20260305-5567, service=export-stream, worker=export-03, size_bytes=2048576, upload=presigned-s3 OK. Upload key `exports/prod/2026-03-05/exp-5567.csv`. Response from S3 included `Content-Type: text/csv` and no `Content-Encoding`.

ben_prodeng: That matches customer seeing `download as .csv`. Why are there gzip bytes inside? Two hypotheses: 1) our streaming pipeline double-encoded a chunk after the refactor (we started compressing intermediate caches), or 2) a partial gzipped chunk from the producer got concatenated to an uncompressed stream. Both would produce embedded gzip headers.

mike_analytics: Reprobed locally: I ran the same query and used curl to hit the presigned URL. `curl -I "<presigned-url>"` returns `Content-Type: text/csv` and `Content-Length: 2048576`. `file downloaded.csv` says `gzip compressed data` when I inspect the file (so S3 object is actually gzipped). But the key name is `.csv` so browser doesn't gunzip. Chrome will download bytes as-is; Excel on Windows expects an unzipped CSV and stops at first NUL.

sarah_support: Customer workaround: Rename file to `.gz` and gunzip, then open CSV. Julie confirms it works. She needs a production fix though. :thumbsup:

ben_prodeng: Noted. I think last export refactor (2026-02-28) started letting worker-side gzip intermediate caches to reduce memory. Bug might be that we upload final object without decompressing/setting proper Content-Encoding. Assigning to me to triage.

ben_prodeng: Quick mitigation we can do server-side: update upload path to set `Content-Encoding: gzip` when object has gzip magic and/or change filename to `.csv.gz`. Either would make browsers or OSes handle it more consistently. I'll push a hotfix to check the uploaded object's first 2 bytes before setting headers.

olga_sre: Can we also surface a temporary message in the UI (Console -> Exports) that shows "If a download opens incorrectly in Excel, try renaming to .gz and gunzip" until fix lands? I can file a small UX ticket.

export-bot: export job exp-20260305-5567 reprocessed by export-03 (attempt 1) — uploaded new object key `exports/prod/2026-03-05/exp-5567.csv.gz` with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and Content-Type `application/gzip`.

mike_analytics: Verified with curl that the new object returns gzip header and the file opens in Excel after gunzip. Also added a unit test to the export-stream that asserts we set `Content-Encoding` when uploading gzipped bodies.

ben_prodeng: Hotfix merged to main (deploy 2026-03-05-15:12), rollback plan ready. I'll follow up with postmortem after full root cause.

sarah_support: Thanks all — Julie confirmed the reprocessed download fixed their problem. Closing ticket after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
